query: Maud's Teacups In Maud's cottage the teacups on the dresser are chiming against each other, all together, though nobody has touched them. Maud pours your tea as if she can't hear a thing. "Biscuit, dearie?" Ask her about the cups "Old cups," says Maud. "Old lake." She looks at the window a long time. "They've done that since I was a girl, on the nights it rings. You get used to it. You don't." Help her wrap them in cloth You wrap every cup in an old tea towel. The chiming stops, and Maud's shoulders come down an inch. "There," she says. "Now we can hear ourselves think."

results.title: Over Many Cups of Tea
results.excerpt:
Over Many Cups of Tea
Maud keeps her word, a little at a time. Over a month of afternoons and more tea than is good for anyone, the story of that spring comes out in pieces: the boathouse, the cold, the friend who didn't come back.
